overview: This single-page Department of State list of papers catalogs two late-1940 communications concerning the governorship of Japanese colonial Taiwan: a telegram from Joseph C. Grew reporting Admiral Kiyoshi Hasegawa’s succession to the resigned Admiral Seizō Kobayashi, and a Navy Department telegram explaining the strategic reasons for appointing an active naval officer. The latter linked Taiwan’s administration to naval cooperation and the anticipated administrative consolidation of Japan’s South Seas Mandate islands with Taiwan, and was cross-referenced to the Pacific War decimal file.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning the Governor of Formosa
subfiles.about: A records-control list summarizes two 1940 telegrams about Admiral Kiyoshi Hasegawa’s appointment as Governor-General of Taiwan and its naval-strategic rationale.
subfiles.summary: The first listed paper is Joseph C. Grew’s November 26, 1940 telegram reporting that Admiral Kiyoshi Hasegawa would succeed the resigned Admiral Kobayashi as Governor-General of Formosa, with comments on Hasegawa’s retention of active-duty status. The second is a December 1 Navy Department telegram explaining that an active naval officer was needed to coordinate the navy with the South Seas administration. It anticipates the possible consolidation of the Japanese-mandated islands’ administration with Taiwan and records a cross-reference to the Pacific War file 740.0011.

interest: The page is useful because it exposes the filing relationships between diplomatic reporting, naval policy, colonial governance, and Pacific War planning. Particularly notable is the Navy Department’s expectation that Japan might combine the administration of its South Seas Mandate islands with Taiwan, placing Hasegawa’s appointment within a broader project of southward strategic integration. The retrospective Department of State list also preserves references to underlying telegrams that may be filed elsewhere or missing from this bundle.
